title: Generic fibre and function field of a surjective integral finite etale cover
statement: Let $X,Z$ be integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $f:Z\to X$ be finite etale and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Put $F=k(X)$ and $L=k(Z)$ [def-sc-function-field]. The morphism induces a finite separable field extension $L/F$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. There is a canonical isomorphism $Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}F\cong\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product] whose projections are the generic-point map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z$ (the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta_Z)\to Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], where $\kappa(\eta_Z)=\mathcal O_{Z,\eta_Z}=L$ because this local ring is a field) and the field-extension map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. More precisely, for every nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, its inverse image is a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $A\to B$ is injective, and the germ maps identify $F=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}B$. Using tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], writing $S=A\setminus\{0\}$, there are compatible $F$-algebra isomorphisms $B\otimes_A F\cong S^{-1}B\cong L$; the first sends $b\otimes(a/s)$ to $ab/s$, and the second sends $b/s$ to its quotient in $L$. These identifications are independent of the affine chart and commute with both projections.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), part (2), with Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions); affine generic fibre and localization calculation in the proof of the returned item, step 5.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $W=f^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine and $B$ is a finite $A$-module. Surjectivity [def-weil-surjective-morphism] makes $W$ nonempty. Apply [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] to $V\subseteq X$ and $W\subseteq Z$: both rings are domains; both opens contain the respective generic points; and the generic germ maps identify $F=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}B$.

source.place: Tag 01WH, definition-integral; Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, integral case; the affine-stalk calculation of schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves (01HV).

proof.text: Write $\varphi:A\to B$ for the affine ring map. Surjectivity gives a point of $W$ over the generic point $(0)$ of $V$. By the spectrum construction [def-weil-affine-spectrum], its prime $\mathfrak q$ has $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=(0)$. Thus $\varphi(a)=0$ implies $a\in(0)$, proving injectivity. Consequently the generic prime $(0)$ of $B$ also contracts to $(0)$ of $A$, so $f(\eta_Z)=\eta_X$. The canonical generic stalk map $\iota:F\to L$ of [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map] satisfies $\iota(g_X(a)/g_X(s))=g_Z(\varphi(a))/g_Z(\varphi(s))$ for $s\ne0$: stalk maps take the germ of a section to the germ of its pullback and preserve inverses. It is injective, since a unital map of fields has zero kernel. This fixes the field embedding used below.

source.place: Tag 0CC1, lemma-dominant-between-integral, proof: generic primes and contraction; the generic stalk map and naturality of germs.

proof.text: The restriction $W\to V$ is etale by [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] with $\mathfrak q=(0)\subset B$ and $\mathfrak p=(0)\subset A$, whose contraction equality was proved in step 2. Their residue fields are $\operatorname{Frac}B=L$ and $\operatorname{Frac}A=F$. The induced residue-field map sends $a/s$ to $\varphi(a)/\varphi(s)$, hence is exactly $\iota$ by step 2. The cited lemma therefore proves that this particular $L/F$ is finite separable.

source.place: Tag 02GJ, lemma-etale-characterize, final assertion; Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field (2), equivalently algebra-lemma-etale-at-prime (00U4).

proof.text: Put $S=A\setminus\{0\}$ and $C=\varphi(S)^{-1}B$. Since $B$ is a domain and $\varphi$ is injective, fractions give an injective map $j:C\to L$, $b/s\mapsto g_Z(b)/g_Z(\varphi(s))$: its kernel is zero because a zero quotient has zero numerator. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] also gives $F\to C$, $a/s\mapsto\varphi(a)/s$, and $j$ respects $F$ by step 2. If $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate the finite $A$-module $B$, then their images span $C$ over $F$: writing $b=\sum a_i b_i$ gives $b/s=\sum(a_i/s)(b_i/1)$. Thus $C$ is a finite-dimensional domain over $F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] to conclude that $C$ is a field. Every nonzero $b\in B$ now has an inverse in $C$. By the same localization universal property, the map $B\to C$ extends to $L=\operatorname{Frac}B\to C$. Its composites with $j$ are identities, since on each fraction $b/t$ both composites return $b/t$. Hence $j:C\cong L$ is the required $F$-algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization; fraction relation preceding Definition 00CO; finite-dimensional-domain argument (rank-nullity) as stated by the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: The compatible maps $B\to C$ and $F\to C$ give, by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], a ring homomorphism $\alpha:B\otimes_A F\to C$ with $\alpha(b\otimes(a/s))=\varphi(a)b/s$. Conversely every $1\otimes s$ for $s\in S$ is invertible, with inverse $1\otimes(1/s)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] to $B\to B\otimes_A F$ to obtain $\beta:C\to B\otimes_A F$, $b/s\mapsto b\otimes(1/s)$. The composite $\alpha\beta$ sends every $b/s$ to itself. On pure tensors, $\beta\alpha(b\otimes(a/s))=\varphi(a)b\otimes(1/s)=b\otimes(a/s)$ by the balancing relation. Pure tensors generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so $\beta\alpha$ is the identity. Both maps preserve the structural $F$-maps, proving the asserted $F$-algebra isomorphism with the stated formula.

source.place: Tag 00DK, lemma-tensor-localization, explicit fraction formula and inverse; Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization.

proof.text: Let $i_X=j_{\eta_X}:\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$ and $i_Z=j_{\eta_Z}:\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z$ be the canonical morphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]; here $\kappa(\eta_X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_X}=F$ and $\kappa(\eta_Z)=L$, since these local rings are fields (step 1), so the residue maps are identities. By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] applied to $f$ and $\eta_Z$, $f i_Z=i_X\operatorname{Spec}(r)$, where $r:\kappa(\eta_X)\to\kappa(\eta_Z)$ is the residue-field map of $f$; as the local rings are these fields, $r$ is the stalk map $\iota$ of step 2, so $f i_Z=i_X\operatorname{Spec}\iota$. The same lemma for the open immersion $V\subseteq X$, together with [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] for $\mathfrak p=(0)\subset A$, shows that $i_X$ factors through $V$ as $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the germ map $A\to\operatorname{Frac}A=F$, $a\mapsto g_X(a)$; likewise the factorization of $i_Z$ through $W$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(g_Z:B\to L)$. The pair $(i_Z,\operatorname{Spec}\iota)$ defines $h:\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}F$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $i_X$ factors through $V$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] and the fibre-product universal property identify this target with $W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}F$: any pair over $X$ factors uniquely through $W=f^{-1}V$, with the same projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] it is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A F)$, its projections corresponding to $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $u\mapsto1\otimes u$. Under this description $h$ is the spectrum of $j\alpha$, $b\otimes u\mapsto g_Z(b)\iota(u)$, an isomorphism by steps 4 and 5. Therefore $h$ is an isomorphism, and its inverse is the displayed generic-fibre isomorphism in the statement. By its defining projection equations it identifies the two projections with $i_Z$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\iota$.

source.place: Tags 01I4/01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes and lemma-fibre-product-affines; Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product; the universal property in Definition 01JP.

proof.text: The fields and maps $\iota,i_X,i_Z$ were defined on generic stalks, independent of a chart. On every nonempty affine chart the ring isomorphism just constructed sends $b\otimes u$ to $g_Z(b)\iota(u)$, so its spectrum is the same morphism $h$: [def-pc-fibre-product] says that a morphism to the pullback is uniquely determined by its two projections. Thus different charts give identical $h$ and identical inverse isomorphisms. More explicitly, on any smaller nonempty affine chart restrictions of $b$ have the same germ in $L$; denominators have the same inverse there, so $b/s\mapsto g_Z(b)/g_Z(\varphi(s))$ agrees with restriction. Two arbitrary charts contain the generic points; choose an affine neighbourhood inside their nonempty intersection and apply these equations twice. This proves chart independence and compatibility with both projections, without assuming intersections of affine opens are affine.
